summary: A news-style feature on the rapid rise of genetic engineering and designer organisms since CRISPR-Cas9 in 2012. It covers milestones from a photosynthetic rodent to drought-tolerant plants, disease-resistant livestock, Huntington's disease correction, plastic-eating bacteria, heat-tolerant coral and space crops. It also highlights the ethical debate, including the Geneva summit and the proposed GeneGuard safeguard.
one_line: Feature on the 2023-2024 genetic engineering boom, from a photosynthetic rodent to plastic-eating bacteria, and the ethical frameworks governing designer organisms.
key_facts: CRISPR-Cas9 was discovered in 2012 and moved from the lab bench to practical application.
On September 5, 2023, Dr. Elaine Simmons of Innovative Genomics Institute announced 'The Second Genesis Project'.
Simmons' team created 'Helios', a small photosynthetic rodent that derives a portion of its energy from sunlight.
CRISPR-Cas9 works as a molecular scissor: the Cas9 enzyme is guided by an RNA piece matching the target DNA sequence and snips the DNA at that location.
In October 2023, Hungarian firm HelixCraft Innovations unveiled a plant that grows in arid conditions, needs minimal water and can purify saline sources.
A consortium led by agricultural scientist Dr. Amardeep Chaudhry developed livestock with improved disease resistance against common pathogens.
On February 9, 2024, a GeneTherapix team led by Dr. Laura Vázquez corrected the genetic mutations responsible for Huntington's disease in vitro.
Genetically engineered viruses are being used as vectors for vaccine delivery, tailored to each pathogen.
The International Summit on Gene Editing was held on March 28, 2024, in Geneva, bringing together ethicists, scientists and policymakers.
Bioethicist Dr. Kiyoko Tanaka conceived 'GeneGuard', a proposed genetic circuitbreaker to stop modified genes from propagating beyond intended boundaries.
On November 10, 2024, startup BioSynthetica announced bacteria that break down plastics into harmless byproducts, a process called 'bio-recycling'.
Marine biologists engineered coral species to withstand warmer ocean temperatures.
NASA and the European Space Agency are collaborating on 'celestial crops' designed to grow in Martian soil simulants.
